items.title: Artemis II crew to hold press conference from deep space tonight

featured_image.name: WATCH: NASA holds daily Artemis II news conference after releasing ...

items.description:
Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are coasting back toward Earth on Wednesday after completing a record-breaking lunar flyby, with the crew scheduled to hold their first in-space press conference later tonight as they near the end of a 10-day voyage around the moon.

The 20-minute virtual news conference is set for 9:45 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 8, with NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, answering media questions from roughly 200,000 miles away.[1]

items.title: UAE demands Iran pay reparations after 40 days of attacks

featured_image.name: UAE has an active role in Iran war and will be pounded if US ...

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates on Wednesday demanded that Iran be held "accountable and fully liable for damages and reparations" following weeks of devastating aerial attacks, as Abu Dhabi sought clarity on the terms of a fragile two-week ceasefire announced by President Donald Trump.

In an official statement, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the "unprovoked Iranian attacks targeting infrastructure, energy facilities, and civilian sites over the past 40 days — which included 2,819 ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones — and the resulting loss of life and property damage, necessitate a firm position". The ministry said it was seeking clarification from Washington on the ceasefire's provisions to ensure "Iran's full commitment to an immediate cessation of all hostilities in the region and the complete and unconditional reopening of the Strait of Hormuz".[1]

items.title: Iran recloses Strait of Hormuz, threatening U.S. ceasefire

featured_image.name: Iran's parliament backs blocking Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
Iran shut down the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, less than 24 hours after agreeing to a two-week ceasefire with the United States, casting immediate doubt over whether the fragile truce that ended more than five weeks of war could survive. Tehran cited Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon as a violation of the agreement, while Washington called the closure "completely unacceptable."[1][2]

The ceasefire, brokered with Pakistan's help and announced Tuesday evening just hours before a deadline set by President Donald Trump, had hinged on what the U.S. described as the "complete, immediate, and safe opening" of the strait — a waterway responsible for roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply. Iran confirmed it would allow passage "in coordination with Iranian armed forces," but Israeli strikes on Beirut that killed more than 100 people overnight appeared to upend that commitment.[3][4][5]

items.title: Israel kills 254 in largest Lebanon strikes as ceasefire dispute erupts

featured_image.name: Aftermath of Israel's heaviest attacks in Lebanon conflict

items.description: Israel unleashed its most devastating wave of airstrikes on Lebanon on Wednesday, killing at least 254 people and wounding more than 1,160 others in what the Israeli military called its "largest coordinated wave of strikes" since the war began on March 2, according to Lebanon's Civil Defence. The assault, which struck over 100 targets across the country within 10 minutes, came just hours after a U.S.-Iran ceasefire took effect — and amid sharp disagreement over whether Lebanon was included in the deal.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: UK vows to restore shipping confidence in Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran ceasefire

featured_image.name: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer arrives in Saudi Arabia ...

items.description:
British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper announced on Wednesday that the United Kingdom will work with the shipping, insurance, and energy sectors to restore confidence in the Strait of Hormuz "as quickly as possible" following a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran.[1][2]

"Iran must cease all mining, drone attacks, and other attempts to block commercial shipping in the Strait immediately," Cooper said in her statement.[3][4]

items.title: NATO chief Rutte meets Trump amid US threat to leave alliance

featured_image.name: Trump is expected to meet with Rutte as he muses about pulling out ...

items.description:
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte arrived at the White House on Wednesday for what may be the most consequential meeting in the alliance's 77-year history, as President Donald Trump's threats to withdraw the United States from the military bloc have plunged transatlantic relations into uncharted territory.

The meeting, confirmed by NATO and the Associated Press, comes after Trump told Reuters and The Telegraph in recent interviews that he is "absolutely" considering pulling the US out of NATO, citing what he called "disgust" with the alliance over European members' refusal to support the US-Israeli air campaign against Iran, launched on February 28. "I was never swayed by NATO," Trump said. "I always knew they were a paper tiger, and Putin knows that too, by the way."[1][2]

items.title: Israeli strike kills Al Jazeera journalist in Gaza

featured_image.name: 🇵🇸🇮🇱 Al Jazeera condemned the deliberate targeting of their journalist  Mohammed Wishah, who was killed in an Israeli drone strike west of Gaza.  They call it a “heinous crime” and part of

items.description: Israeli forces killed at least 10 Palestinians in Gaza on Tuesday and carried out further strikes on Wednesday, including one that killed Al Jazeera correspondent Mohammed Wishah, as the U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement continues to unravel six months after it took effect.

items.title: Vance to lead US delegation in Iran talks in Islamabad

featured_image.name: US Vice President Vance spoke to intermediaries about Iran ...

items.description: The United States and Iran are preparing for their first face-to-face negotiations since the outbreak of war, with Vice President JD Vance set to lead the American delegation to Islamabad this weekend for talks aimed at forging a lasting peace agreement. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf will head Tehran's team, according to Iran's semi-official ISNA news agency. The high-stakes diplomacy follows a two-week ceasefire agreed to on Tuesday night, brokered largely through Pakistan's mediation.[1][2]

items.title: UN envoy arrives in Iran amid fragile US ceasefire

featured_image.name: UN chief names Arnault as ME envoy

items.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres's personal envoy Jean Arnault has arrived in Iran as part of a regional tour aimed at supporting "a comprehensive and durable resolution" to the conflict engulfing the Middle East, the United Nations announced on Wednesday. The visit comes amid a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran brokered just one day earlier with Pakistan's mediation.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran’s parliament speaker says cease-fire terms already violated

featured_image.name: Israel continues its attacks on Dahieh district in Beirut

items.description: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Wednesday that three clauses of Tehran's 10-point ceasefire framework have already been violated, casting doubt over the fragile truce reached just hours earlier between the United States and Iran. The accusation came as Israel launched what its military called its largest wave of strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon since the war began, hitting 100 targets in 10 minutes.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump sends Vance, Witkoff, Kushner to Islamabad for Iran talks

featured_image.name: Iran War Latest: Vance, Witkoff, Kushner Heading to Pakistan for Peace  Talks - Bloomberg

items.description:
President Donald Trump is dispatching a high-level delegation led by Vice President JD Vance to Islamabad for face-to-face negotiations with Iran, the White House announced Wednesday, just hours after a fragile two-week ceasefire halted 38 days of U.S. and Israeli military operations against Tehran.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed the team. "I can announce that the president is dispatching his negotiating team, led by the vice president of the United States, JD Vance, Special Envoy Witkoff and Mr. Kushner to Islamabad for talks this weekend," she said. "The first round of those talks will take place on Saturday morning local time."[1]

items.title: 289-million-year-old mummy reveals oldest rib-based breathing

featured_image.name: Mummified reptile hints at the origins of how we breathe

items.description: A tiny mummified reptile that died in an Oklahoma cave roughly 289 million years ago has yielded the oldest known evidence of rib-based breathing in amniotes — the group encompassing all reptiles, birds, and mammals — according to a study published Wednesday in Nature.[1][2]

items.title: Iran faces economic collapse after 40 days of war

featured_image.name: Even if Iran's regime outlasts Trump, it may not survive ...

items.description: Iran emerged from 40 days of U.S.-Israeli bombardment this week with a two-week ceasefire in hand but an economy in ruins. In interviews with Iranian political insiders, business owners, and analysts, Reuters charted a country "near the brink of economic collapse," warning that any military gains Tehran secured during the conflict may prove fleeting.[1]

items.title: Iran threatens to quit ceasefire after Israel's massive Lebanon strikes

featured_image.name: Israel says Iran ceasefire doesn't apply to Lebanon, and strikes central Beirut without warning

items.description: A fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran, brokered by Pakistan and announced late Tuesday, was thrust into crisis on Wednesday as Iran warned it may withdraw from the agreement following Israel's largest coordinated wave of strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon since the war began in late February.

items.title: Israel learned of Iran cease-fire deal at last minute

featured_image.name: Netanyahu says announcement of Gaza ceasefire's next phase is ...

items.description:
Israel was not formally part of the negotiations that produced the two-week cease-fire between the United States and Iran announced on Tuesday, and Israeli officials were unhappy to learn that a deal had been finalized without prior consultation, according to a Wall Street Journal exclusive report citing mediators and a person familiar with the matter.[1]

The extent of Israel's involvement amounted to a phone call from President Donald Trump to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shortly before the cease-fire was publicly announced, a White House official told the Journal. Netanyahu agreed to participate in the cease-fire during that call.[1]

items.title: Meta unveils Muse Spark, its first AI model from superintelligence team

featured_image.name: Meta announces new AI model that can generate video with sound

items.description: Meta on Wednesday unveiled Muse Spark, the first artificial intelligence model produced by its superintelligence division, marking the company's most substantial AI release in over a year as it races to close a gap with rivals OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google. The model, developed over roughly nine months under the internal codename Avocado, is now powering the Meta AI app and website in the United States, with a broader rollout planned in the coming weeks across Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp, and Meta's smart glasses.[1][2][3]

items.title: Ceasefire frays as Iran strikes Gulf states, refinery hit

featured_image.name: Iran hits Kuwaiti oil refinery, blasts boom over Tehran

items.description:
The ink was barely dry on the two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran when fresh violence erupted across the Middle East on Wednesday, underscoring the fragility of an agreement reached just hours before President Trump's deadline threatening the destruction of Iranian "civilization."[1][2]

Iran launched a wave of missiles and drones at targets in the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait early Wednesday, claiming retaliation for a strike on its oil facilities, according to Al Jazeera. The UAE Defense Ministry said its air defenses were "actively engaging" Iranian ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones, while Kuwait reported intercepting 28 Iranian drones targeting oil facilities, power plants, and water desalination sites, with some causing infrastructure damage. Separately, Iran's state-owned refiner NIORDC confirmed that a 55,000-barrel-per-day refinery on Lavan Island was struck in what it called a "cowardly attack by enemies" around 10 a.m. local time Wednesday, though no casualties were reported.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Oman rejects Iran's Hormuz toll plan in ceasefire dispute

featured_image.name: Oman rejects Iran's Hormuz toll demand. Can such fees be levied on ...

items.description: Iran's push to charge vessels up to $2 million each for transiting the Strait of Hormuz has become one of the most contentious elements of the two-week ceasefire agreed with the United States on Tuesday, drawing sharp opposition from Oman, Gulf states, and international legal experts who say the fees violate maritime law.

items.title: Vance calls Iran ceasefire 'fragile,' set to lead talks Friday

featured_image.name: US proposes replacing Witkoff with JD Vance on negotiating team ...

items.description:
US Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday described the newly struck ceasefire between the United States and Iran as a "fragile truce," urging Tehran to negotiate in good faith and warning that President Donald Trump is "not one to mess around."

Speaking at the Mathias Corvinus Collegium in Budapest during a two-day visit to Hungary, Vance said Trump is "impatient to make progress" and that Iran faces serious consequences if it does not engage sincerely in upcoming talks.[1][2]

"If the Iranians are willing in good faith to work with us, I think we can make an agreement," Vance said. But he cautioned: if Iran refuses to come to the negotiating table, "they're going to find out that the President of the United States is not one to mess around".[1]

items.title: NYT names Adam Back as likely Bitcoin creator Satoshi Nakamoto

featured_image.name: Adam Back Said It’s Still Early For The Retail Investors To Buy Bitcoin

items.description: The New York Times published an investigation on Wednesday naming British cryptographer Adam Back, 55, as the most likely person behind Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator Satoshi Nakamoto — a mystery that has persisted for 17 years since the cryptocurrency's launch. Back has repeatedly denied the claim.
